subject.title: feat(onboarding): recommend plugins and skills from installed apps

question: Should classic macOS onboarding transmit detected application names to the configured model and ClawHub by default after an in-progress disclosure, or require explicit consent before the first network request?
rationale: This is a privacy and trust-policy choice affecting default onboarding behavior and external data transmission; repository evidence can identify the boundary but cannot decide the intended product promise.

options.title: Consent Before Sharing
options.body: Scan locally if desired, but ask before sending any app names or bundle identifiers to the model or ClawHub, with decline preserving normal onboarding.

options.title: Keep Default-On Disclosure
options.body: Explicitly accept the current default-on behavior as product policy, strengthen the disclosure, and still remove filesystem paths from the node payload.

options.title: Local-Only Recommendations
options.body: Use official local catalog matching by default and make model or ClawHub enrichment a separately selected online step.

recommendation.title: Consent Before Sharing
recommendation.body: Scan locally if desired, but ask before sending any app names or bundle identifiers to the model or ClawHub, with decline preserving normal onboarding.

likelyOwner.reason: The branch explicitly attributes the current default-on consent model to a deliberate onboarding product decision owned in this area.
